content: Ampicillin trihydrate should be administered with specific dosages and schedules depending on the patient’s age, weight, and the type of infection being treated. Below are the detailed instructions for its use: Adults and Children Weighing Over 20 kg: 1. For genitourinary or gastrointestinal tract infections (excluding gonorrhea): The standard dose is 500 mg four times daily (q.i.d.) at evenly spaced intervals. Severe or chronic infections may necessitate higher doses. For gonorrhea, a single dose of 5 grams of ampicillin combined with 1 gram of probenecid is recommended. Physicians are advised not to use less than this dosage for gonorrhea treatment. 2. Follow-up for gonorrhea treatment: Cultures should be obtained from the original infection site(s) 7 to 14 days after completing therapy. In women, it is also recommended to perform test-of-cure cultures from both the endocervical and anal canals. Complications such as prostatitis and epididymitis require prolonged and intensive therapy. 3. For respiratory tract infections: The usual dose is 250 mg four times daily (q.i.d.) at evenly spaced intervals. Children Weighing 20 kg or Less: 1. For genitourinary or gastrointestinal tract infections: The standard dose is 100 mg/kg/day, divided into four equal doses (q.i.d.) administered at evenly spaced intervals. 2. For respiratory tract infections: The usual dose is 50 mg/kg/day, divided into three or four equal doses administered at evenly spaced intervals. 3. General considerations for pediatric dosing: The dosage for children should not exceed the recommended adult dosage. All Patients (Regardless of Age or Weight): 1. Severe or chronic infections: Larger doses may be required. 2. Administration timing: Although ampicillin is resistant to degradation by gastric acid, it should be taken at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after meals to ensure optimal absorption. 3. Duration of therapy: Except for the single-dose regimen for gonorrhea, treatment should continue for at least 48 to 72 hours after the patient becomes asymptomatic or after evidence of bacterial eradication is obtained. For infections caused by hemolytic strains of streptococci, a minimum of 10 days of treatment is recommended to prevent complications such as rheumatic fever or glomerulonephritis. 4. Chronic urinary or gastrointestinal infections: Frequent bacteriologic and clinical evaluations are necessary during therapy and may need to continue for several months afterward. Persistent infections may require treatment for several weeks. 5. Dosage caution: Smaller doses than those specified above should not be used. These guidelines ensure the effective use of ampicillin trihydrate while minimizing the risk of treatment failure or complications.
